model_check: The conditional theorem is stated for a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm that halts on every execution, answers correctly with probability at least 2/3, and uses O(2^(T'n)) word operations on every input of n integers whose bit lengths and target are at most n^c, for every fixed c, in the word-RAM model of the OpenAI paper (paper, Theorem 1 and Section 1). Source comparison, not a proof check; the word length is the OpenAI paper's and is not restated in the theorem.

verification: Conditional on the non-numerical lemmas of the OpenAI paper and of Annanay Kapila's written proof (Base), the same premises as the Wharton 0.487676 and Bills 0.4876723 rows. The author certifies the 33 numerical conditions of Base's proof at new parameters with one asymmetric filter (16 cosine and 16 sine terms) in place of Base's 43 cosine-only filters, in ball arithmetic with at least two independent implementations, and re-derives Base's probabilistic core. The paper says it is not peer reviewed and claims no Lean proof and no unconditional theorem. The theorem gives O(2^(T'n)) for every T' > T = 0.4875754036 and, in particular, O(2^(0.4875755n)); T is tau_0 = 0.4875752036 plus 20 eps with eps = 1e-8 (paper, Section 8). The same paper also states a ternary-mask exponent 0.4873407528 that needs an unproved statement [S]; it is not part of the claim and is not listed. No Big O Speedrun proof check. Evidence remains Claimed.
